newsitem.title: USA: Boston Housing Auth might lose $50 mln funds - paper.
newsitem.headline: Boston Housing Auth might lose $50 mln funds - paper.

text.p: The Boston Housing Authority is at risk of losing $50 million in federal funds to renovate the Mission Main public housing development due to an ongoing feud with developers and tenants, the Boston Globe said Tuesday.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development found the city in default on the project and warned that funding will be withdrawn unless the Authority, developers and tenants reach agreement by the end of this week.
The paper said that this is the second time the federal agency has threatened to withdraw funding to Boston for the Mission Main Housing project.

After the first warning in late 1995, the Authority reorganized its staff and promised to break ground on Mission Main in the autumn of 1996. The federal agency said the project at present is five months behind that revised schedule.

The funds from Washington are supposed to be used to build 535 new apartments at Mission Main, and the project was supposed to cost $107 million, according to the developers' account, the paper said. Tenants are siding with the developers team.

But the Authority's Administrator, Sandra Henriquez says she cannot justify using Washington's $50 million grant and $40 million in tax credits to build housing that she says will cost $187,000 per unit. The Massachusetts Housing Finance Agency sets $149,000 per unit as an upper limit for its projects.
Boston's mayor, Thomas Menino on Monday called his chief of staff and the Boston Redevelopment Authority director to help Henriquez iron out an agreement, the Globe said.
